text: In the city of Veyr, every choice is written down. Every purchase. Every passage. Every promise. Privacy became evidence of guilt.
So the Night Runners built the Veil: a way to lock a choice in public without revealing it. Commit before the final bell. Reveal only when no one can change course.

Veil Vault is a four-runner bluffing game. Three vaults hold three, five, and eight relics. Choose one door and hope no rival chooses it too. A shared door wakes the alarm. The highest lone claim wins.
This is the practice chamber. No wallet, no account, no payment. Just four runners, three vaults, and one hidden choice.
First, the briefing. Three relics are about to burn. Your rivals have already sealed their moves, so the house cannot react to yours.
Choose a vault. Copper is the quiet three. Moon is the middle five. The Sun Crown is worth eight, and everyone sees it. Read the tendencies, then trust your read.

Seal your move. Your choice is mixed with a random secret and hashed into a commitment. Four commitments go public. Zero choices. Keep the receipt private; it is the key that opens your commitment later.

When the veil lifts, every runner reveals. The browser checks each reveal against its commitment, then recomputes the round. A forged winner is rejected. This is browser-side verification, not on-chain verification.
The same commit-then-reveal pattern can travel through Zcash. The testnet lab prepares shielded wallet requests. Your wallet signs; the site never sees keys. No live testnet round has been run.
Browser practice, not chain evidence. The audit demo uses fabricated sample records, and the site keeps no accounts, analytics, cookies, or browser storage.
Play the practice vault. Choose a vault. Keep it hidden. veil-vault-game.vercel.app.
